name: 2027 Prairie Avenue: the brick barn on the alley, K12

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2027, uncrossed, and letters it BARN. Unlike its GARAGE neighbours, BARN is a horse-era word, but it is still the 1911 sheet's and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2027-rear). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: two carriage bays, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the first of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft. The sheet census (census row s35-2027-rear, trace s35fp-2027-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (9.75 x 12.75 m inside 84% of the trace): the sheet draws a building 10.73 m deep from the alley line and 14.53 m along it, its north wall on the 2021/2027 lot line against 2021's one-storey brick building and its south wall 0.49 m inside the 2027/2031 line, clear of 2031's garage. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

position.note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1170.89, 721.00): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 695-750 (peak at column 1170.89), halfway between the north wall line (row 681.91, a profile over columns 1120-1160; the 2021/2027 lot line west of the building reads row 681.87 on the same rule, so the wall is on the lot line) and the south wall line (row 760.08, columns 1120-1160; the 2027/2031 lot line west of the building reads 762.70), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1470.151, N -3565.437. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2027, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.611 degrees, the draft's 179.389 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed. The draft's fitted rectangle (9.75 x 12.75 m) had its rear corner 6.22 m north and 0.83 m west of this wall's middle.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (1170.89, 721.00) of the committed sheet 35 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1170.89) back to its west wall line (column 1113.16, a profile over rows 695-750): 57.73 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 10.729 m; and from its north wall line (row 681.91) to its south wall line (row 760.08): 78.17 pixels, 14.528 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner, under its north wall line. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under the kit's 40-degree roof (4.50 m from eave to ridge over the 10.73 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick and the window mark's place is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2027-barn-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label BARN, the north wall on the 2021/2027 lot line where 2021's one-storey brick building stands against it, the south wall 0.49 m inside the 2027/2031 line, and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall 7.54 m from the north wall. The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east) and built in mirror image so that its party wall stands at the north end, on the lot line it shares with 2021's building, as 1834's does against 1828's (L-k12-1834-stable-1935); the open gable faces south over the half-metre gap to 2031's garage and carries no opening, since nothing could be reached or lit across it. On the alley wall, counted from the party wall's inner face: a carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch and hoist over it, a man door, the mark built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, and a second carriage bay with a loft sash over it. On the yard wall three stable sash with loft sash over them and a door where the walk from the house meets it. The kit's gable roof at its own 40 degrees with the ridge along the alley, 4.50 m from eave to ridge over the 10.73 m span; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. The workyard is paved from the yard door 6.92 m west to the east face of the house's one-storey frame back porch (sheet column 1075.93, rows 745.4-761.5). No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
